chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best speech.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The meaning of His Words,
is the standing of the man from his bed, intending Allah by it, not intending anything else by it.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'best speech' mean in the context of night prayer?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'aqwam qilan' (most upright in speech/conduct) is interpreted not merely as rhetorical clarity, but as the physical and spiritual act of rising from one's bed for night prayer with pure monotheistic intent (ikhlas). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal state of devotion accompanying the external ritual, linking the physical effort of Tahajjud directly to the purity of one's relationship with Allah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [73:6] Surely the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best speech. Heasws said: ‘The Meaning of Hisazwj Words
is the standing of the man from his bed intending Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by it, not intending anything else by it’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘nightly initiation is of strong impression and of strongest words’ [73:7] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, “‘strongest words”
means a man’s getting up from his bed just for the sake of Allah and for no other considerations.’”
